title: Should her squares pay more than the robot's own?
question: After the hoe landed, the robot earned every point on soil it had opened itself and never watered her sown field. The chief of staff asked whether a tile she planted should pay more than one the robot tilled.
why_now: It was the next reward value to set. The CEO answered by replacing the question.

options.label: Her sown tile pays more
options.detail: A sown tile 1.0, an empty tilled tile less. Rejected: it invents ownership of tiles.

options.label: Reward every beneficial thing, and nobody owns a tile (the CEO's answer)
options.detail: Mailbox 10, crow off food 3, crow flying in 1, harvest 1, water a thirsty plant 1, plant 1, till grass 0.1, water empty soil 0.1.

ruled.summary: There is no distinction of who owns a tile. The robot is rewarded for beneficial things, on the full table: mailbox 10, crow off food 3, crow flying in 1, harvest 1, water a thirsty plant 1, plant 1, till grass 0.1, water empty soil 0.1. With exploration preserved and an efficient learner, these parameters alone should yield a robust robot for the game as built.
